purpose: K4 (b)-(d): growth of the amplitude-weighted frequency centroid with the grid size N, for a one-dimensional sine, a single-octave product field and the canonical four-octave sum field, with integer and non-integer f, five values of gamma, and three edge treatments (no window, Hann window, periodic field via integer f). The conjectured exponent min(1, 1.5 - 1/gamma) for the two-dimensional sum field is tested with the rejection criterion below. Supplies the numbers for Appendix B and Fig. 4.
fixed_before_running: Written on 2026-10-25, before any computation in this file. Any condition added or removed after seeing results is listed under 'deviations' with its reason, and the version number is increased. A timing run (about 2 s per field at N = 4096) was used only to estimate the computational cost; its values were not used to choose conditions.

fields.name: sum
fields.rule: Canonical field (S1.2: four-octave sum; S1.4: maxabs normalisation). Primary object.

fields.name: product1
fields.rule: Single-octave product field (octaves = 1). Control with straight zero lines.

fields.name: oned
fields.rule: One-dimensional sine sin(2 pi f x + phi), phi uniform from default_rng(seed).uniform(0, 2 pi); centroid as in S2.7. Numerical control for the propositions of Appendix A.

f_note: The rule's range is f in [3, 7]. Integer f is the 'periodised' case (S1.6). f = 6.3 represents a fractional part other than 1/2.
gamma_note: The rule's range is gamma in [0.9, 2.6]. gamma = 1 makes T_gamma the identity; with integer f the field is then band-limited (control).
height: H = T_gamma(F) with s = 1 (s does not affect the centroid; S2.2).

descriptors.name: centroid_power
descriptors.rule: Power weighting of S2.4 over the full band. Check of K4 (d).

descriptors.name: centroid_band_power
descriptors.rule: Band-fixed centroid of S2.4 with K = 32 cycles per domain and power weighting. Check of K4 (d).

aliasing.rule: S4: generate H (after T_gamma) on a fine grid, apply the ideal low-pass and decimate (decimate_fourier), and compare with direct sampling. Primary: fixed r = 2 for every N (so that the reference does not change with N). Convergence check: r = 4 for N <= 2048; the difference between r = 2 and r = 4 is reported as the residual aliasing of the reference.
aliasing.boundary: decimate_fourier treats the fine array as periodic. For non-integer f the fine array is not periodic, so the low-pass also acts on the edge discontinuity; this is reported, not corrected.
aliasing.subset: Restricted for computational cost to fields = sum, f in {5, 5.5}, all five gamma, seeds 1-10, both processings. The restriction was fixed by cost alone, without looking at values.

slope: S6.1: per seed, least-squares slope of ln C on ln N; mean over seeds and 95% t interval over seeds (19 degrees of freedom).

slope_ranges.local: Slope between each pair of consecutive N (descriptive only).

rejection_criterion.cells: fields = sum, f in {3, 5, 7} (integer, so no edge discontinuity), gamma in {0.9, 1.25, 1.75, 2.6} (gamma != 1), processing = raw, centroid_amp, direct sampling: 12 cells.
rejection_criterion.rule: Decision per cell on the primary range (N 512-4096) with simultaneous intervals: Bonferroni-adjusted t intervals at level 1 - 0.05/12 over seeds. 'Rejected' if at least one cell's adjusted interval excludes e(gamma); the cells and the direction are reported, and the claim withdrawn is the estimate min(1, 1.5 - 1/gamma) as stated in Appendix B (the proven one-dimensional results are not affected). 'Consistent' if every adjusted interval contains e(gamma) on the primary range and also on the sensitivity range N 1024-4096. 'Not decidable in this N range' if the decisions on the primary and the sensitivity ranges differ. In no case is the result reported as a proof.
rejection_criterion.secondary: The same cells are also computed on the decimate_fourier version (f = 5 only). A disagreement with direct sampling is reported as a contribution of aliasing. The decision is made on the primary analysis.
rejection_criterion.sensitivity: The same decision on N in {1024, 2048, 4096} (three points).
rejection_criterion.finite_N_note: Intervals over seeds do not include the systematic bias of a finite N range; local slopes and the log-corrected fit below are reported next to the decision for this reason.

predictions: P-K4-1 (one-dimensional control, Appendix A): for oned, integer f, raw, the slope approaches 1 - 1/gamma for gamma > 1 and is 0 at gamma = 1. For gamma = 0.9 the centroid converges (proved): the local slope tends to 0 (it is not 1 - 1/gamma, which would be negative).
P-K4-2 (product control): for product1 with integer f the slope is close to the one-dimensional exponent 1 - 1/gamma (straight zero lines).

P-K4-3 (sum field, conjecture; gamma != 1 only): for sum with integer f and gamma != 1, the slope exceeds the one-dimensional value and is positive also at gamma = 0.9. Its value is judged by the rejection criterion. (At gamma = 1 both are 0; see P-K4-4.)

P-K4-4 (gamma = 1, integer f): for sum and product1 the centroid does not depend on N for N >= 128 (band-limited; the highest component frequency 7 x 8 = 56 is below N/2 = 64). The slope interval contains 0.

P-K4-5 (edge discontinuity, K4 (c)): for non-integer f, gamma = 1, raw, the centroid grows roughly like N / log N (corollary of the one-dimensional result). The slope is below 1 and approaches 1 as N grows (increasing local slope). Only the direction is predicted, not the value.
P-K4-6 (window): for non-integer f, the hann slope approaches the hann slope of integer f at the same gamma (the edge discontinuity is removed) and is smaller than the raw slope for non-integer f.

P-K4-7 (power weighting, K4 (d)): for integer f, centroid_power converges with N (local slope tends to 0). For non-integer f, raw, centroid_power grows roughly linearly in ln N. centroid_band_power does not depend on N for gamma = 1 and integer f (for gamma != 1, aliasing from outside K = 32 may enter, so no direction is predicted).
readouts: Mean and standard error over seeds of each centroid for every cell (field, f, gamma, processing, descriptor, sampling) and every N.
Slopes over the primary and descriptive ranges (mean and 95% interval) and local slopes.
Table of the decision for the 12 cells of the rejection criterion.
C ln N / N for gamma = 1 and non-integer f (check of P-K4-5).
Paired difference (same seed) between the two sampling methods of the aliasing subset: mean and standard error.
not_done: Direct verification of the zero-line geometry (inflection points, crossings). Warped fields.
log_corrected_fit: Descriptive: per seed, least squares of ln C = a + b ln N + c ln ln N over N 256-4096; mean and t interval of b and c over seeds.
normalisation_check: Control: for fields = sum, f in {5, 5.5}, gamma in {0.9, 1.75}, seeds 1-5, the centroid with maxabs and with ampsum normalisation is compared at every N; they must agree to rounding (S1.4). A disagreement indicates an implementation error, not a finding.
deviations_before_running: 2026-10-25, before any computation: revised after a second opinion (Codex), see the commit message. Changes: simultaneous intervals and a 'not decidable' outcome in the rejection criterion; sensitivity range; log-corrected fit; fixed r = 2 for the aliasing reference with r = 4 as a convergence check; gamma != 1 in P-K4-3; normalisation check.
